guide.intro: Japanese is written with three scripts at once. Hiragana and katakana are sound scripts (46 letters each). Kanji are Chinese-origin characters that each carry a MEANING, so one kanji can replace a whole word. Learning kanji is easier once you know they are built from parts (radicals).

points.note: Kanji give the core meaning of nouns, verbs and adjectives; hiragana adds grammar endings and small words; katakana writes foreign words and emphasis.
points.jp: 私はコーヒーを飲みます。
points.en: I drink coffee. (私, 飲 = kanji; は, を, み, ます = hiragana; コーヒー = katakana)

points.pattern: One kanji = one idea, several readings
points.note: A kanji keeps its meaning but can be read in different ways depending on the word it is in.
points.jp: 山 = やま / サン

points.note: Hiragana that follows a kanji stem to show the verb or adjective ending.
points.jp: 食べる・食べます・食べた
points.en: eat / eats / ate — the kanji stays, the kana changes

points.note: Write top to bottom, left to right. A horizontal line usually comes before a vertical one that crosses it. Outside frames come before insides, and the bottom line of a box is written last.
points.jp: 十・口・国

points.note: About 2,136 common-use (常用) kanji cover newspapers and books. JLPT N5 needs around 100, N4 around 300, N3 around 650.
points.jp: 日・月・火・水・木・金・土
points.en: start with the days of the week

points.note: Most kanji are a radical (meaning hint) plus another part (often a sound hint). Learn the ~57 common radicals and you can guess the topic of thousands of kanji.

guide.intro: Most kanji are built from smaller parts. One of those parts - the radical (部首, bushu) - hints at the meaning. Learn a few dozen radicals and new kanji stop looking like random strokes.

points.note: The radical tells you the topic of the kanji. Water radical 氵 = liquids and seas.
points.jp: 海・泳・洗

points.note: On the side of a kanji some radicals squash: 人→亻, 水→氵, 心→忄, 手→扌, 犬→犭.
points.jp: 休・海・忙・持

points.note: hen (left), tsukuri (right), kanmuri (top), ashi (bottom), tare (hanging), nyō (wrapping), kamae (enclosing).
points.jp: 何・欠・家・思・病・道・国

points.pattern: The other half hints at sound
points.note: In many kanji the non-radical part gives a sound hint. 青 is 'sei' so 静, 晴, 清 are also 'sei'.
points.jp: 青・静・晴

points.note: Each kanji has a Chinese-style reading (on) used in compounds and a Japanese-style reading (kun) used alone with hiragana endings.
points.jp: 水 = スイ / みず

guide.intro: Learn each radical's shape, its Japanese name and its meaning. The quiz also shows you real kanji and asks which radical is inside.

points.note: Person. A squashed version of 人 (a person walking) so it fits on the left side of a kanji. Kanji with it are about people and what people do. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 何 = 亻 + 可

points.pattern: 人  ひと・ひとがしら (hito / hitogashira)
points.note: Person. A picture of a person seen from the side, legs apart. On top of a kanji it looks like a roof (ひとやね). It sits on the TOP like a roof or crown.
points.jp: 人 = 人

points.pattern: 女  おんな・おんなへん (onna)
points.note: Woman. A kneeling woman with folded arms. Appears in kanji about women, family and relatives. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 女 = 女

points.note: Power. A flexed arm muscle. About strength and effort. It sits on the RIGHT of the kanji.
points.jp: 力 = 力

points.pattern: 口  くち・くちへん (kuchi)
points.note: Mouth. A square open mouth. It shows up in kanji about speaking, eating, naming and asking. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 口 = 口

points.note: Inch / measure. A hand with a mark on the wrist to feel the pulse - a small measure. Kanji with it often relate to rules, hands and measuring. It sits at the BOTTOM like legs.
points.jp: 寺 = 土 + 寸

guide.intro: Learn each radical's shape, its Japanese name and its meaning. The quiz also shows you real kanji and asks which radical is inside.

points.note: Heart. A picture of a heart with its chambers. Kanji with it are about feelings and thoughts. It sits at the BOTTOM like legs.
points.jp: 心 = 心

points.note: Heart. 心 stood on its side as a left-hand radical: feelings and states of mind. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 忙 = 忄 + 亡

points.note: Hand. A hand with fingers and wrist. Alone it means hand. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.
points.jp: 手 = 手

points.note: Hand. 手 shortened to fit on the left. Kanji with it are actions done by hand: push, hit, hold, pick. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 持 = 扌 + 寺

points.note: Eye. An eye turned on its side and drawn upright. About seeing and looking. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.
points.jp: 目 = 目

points.note: Flesh / body part. 肉 squeezed into the moon shape. Kanji with it name body parts: back, chest, arm. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 背 = 北 + ⺼

points.note: Sickness. A person lying on a bed under a roof. About illness and pain. It hangs from the top-left and covers the rest.
points.jp: 病 = 疒 + 丙

points.note: Tree. A trunk with branches above and roots below. Kanji with it are about wood, plants and things made of wood. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 木 = 木

points.note: Water. Streams of flowing water. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.

points.note: Water. Three drops of water on the left. Kanji with it are about liquids, seas, rivers and washing. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.

points.note: Fire. Flames rising from a hearth. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.

points.jp: 無 = 無

points.pattern: 土  つち・つちへん (tsuchi)
points.note: Earth. A little plant sprouting from the ground. About soil, land and places. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 土 = 土

points.pattern: 月  つき・つきへん (tsuki)
points.note: Moon. A crescent moon. About the moon, months and time. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 有 = ナ + 月

points.pattern: 山  やま・やまへん (yama)

points.note: Stone. A stone (口) under a cliff (厂). It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.

points.note: Rain. Drops falling from a cloud under the sky line. Weather kanji: snow, electricity. It sits on the TOP like a roof or crown.
points.jp: 雨 = 一 + 冂 + 水

points.note: Grass / plant. Two sprouts (屮 屮) on top of a kanji. Kanji with it name plants, flowers, tea and herbs. It sits on the TOP like a roof or crown.
points.jp: 草 = 艹 + 早

points.pattern: 竹  たけ・たけかんむり (take)

points.jp: 節 = 竹 + 即

points.pattern: 禾  のぎ・のぎへん (nogi)

points.note: Rice field. A field divided into plots by paths. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.

points.note: Jewel / king. Three jade beads on a string. On the left it loses its dot and looks like 王. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.

points.note: King. Three levels - heaven, people, earth - joined by one ruler. As a left radical it means jewel. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 王 = 王

points.note: Dog. A dog with an ear and a tail. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.
points.jp: 犬 = 大 + 丶

points.note: Animal. 犬 on the left. Kanji with it are animals and animal-like traits. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.

points.pattern: 金  かね・かねへん (kane)

points.note: Clothing. 衣 on the left: clothing and dress. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.

points.note: Sword. A blade with a curved back. It can stand alone or fill most of the kanji.
points.jp: 前 = 䒑 + 月 + 刂

points.note: Knife. 刀 stood upright on the right. Kanji with it are about cutting and dividing. It sits on the RIGHT of the kanji.

points.pattern: 弓  ゆみ・ゆみへん (yumi)
points.note: Bow. A bow with a string. About bows, and often 'strong' or 'pull'. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 弟 = 弓 + ノ

points.pattern: 車  くるま・くるまへん (kuruma)
points.note: Vehicle / wheel. A cart seen from above: axle and two wheels. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 車 = 車

points.pattern: 言  ごん・ごんべん (gonben)
points.note: Say / word. A mouth with sound waves rising. Kanji with it are about words, talk and language. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 言 = 口 + 辛

points.note: Show / altar. An altar table where offerings are shown to the gods. It sits on the TOP like a roof or crown.
points.jp: 祭 = 月 + 又 + 示

points.note: Altar / spirit. 示 on the left: gods, festivals and blessings. It sits on the LEFT of the kanji.
points.jp: 礼 = 礻 + 乚

points.note: Roof. The roof of a house. Kanji with it are homes, rooms and shelter. It sits on the TOP like a roof or crown.

points.note: Building / grotto. A roof with a wall on the left. Kanji with it are shops and public buildings. It hangs from the top-left and covers the rest.
points.jp: 広 = 广 + 厶

points.pattern: 尸  しかばね・しゃくかね (shikabane)

guide.intro: Every kanji can have two kinds of readings. The on-yomi (音読み) came from Chinese; the kun-yomi (訓読み) is the original Japanese word for the same idea. Two simple rules tell you which one to use most of the time.

points.note: A kanji standing alone, especially with hiragana after it, is read with the kun-yomi.
points.jp: 水 (みず)・食べる (たべる)・大きい (おおきい)

points.note: In a compound of two or more kanji the on-yomi is usual.
points.jp: 水曜日 (すいようび)・学校 (がっこう)

points.note: Some compounds use kun readings (手紙 てがみ, 朝日 あさひ) and some single kanji use on readings (本 ほん, 力 ちから is kun). Learn them as whole words.
points.jp: 手紙・朝日・本

points.note: The non-radical part of a kanji often tells you the on reading. 青 is 'sei', so 静 晴 清 精 are all 'sei'.
points.jp: 青・静・晴・清・精
points.en: blue, quiet, fine weather, pure, spirit

points.note: 方 is 'hō': 放 訪 房 防 share it. 交 is 'kō': 校 効 郊. 古 is 'ko': 湖 固 個 枯. 同 is 'dō': 洞 胴 銅. 包 is 'hō': 泡 抱 砲.
points.jp: 方・放・訪・防

points.note: Radical tells the topic; the other part tells the sound. 海 = 氵 (water) + 毎 (mai): a water word read 'kai'. It is not perfect, but it makes guessing much easier.
points.jp: 河・湖・油・流
points.en: river, lake, oil, flow - all water words

guide.intro: The て-form joins actions, makes requests and unlocks many patterns. You build it from the dictionary form, and the ending decides how.
